title: The animal life cycle
summary: Practise how animals are born and grow.
keyIdeas: All animals are born, grow and die. They may reproduce.
Some animals hatch from eggs. Others are born from their mother's body.
Animals such as frogs and butterflies change a lot as they grow.

basicKnowledge: A. Cultura científica › La vida en nuestro planeta
A. Cultura científica › Iniciación en la actividad científica

activities.prompt: Animals are born, grow and may reproduce.
activities.explanation: A life cycle includes birth, growth, possible reproduction and death. Not every animal has young.

activities.prompt: Lucía sees a nest. Where do baby sparrows come from?
activities.explanation: Sparrows are birds. They hatch from eggs laid by their mothers.
activities.hint: Think about how birds are born.

activities.prompt: Put the frog's life cycle in order.
activities.explanation: A frog hatches from an egg. It is first a tadpole, then a young frog.

activities.prompt: Match each animal to its young.
activities.explanation: Young animals have different names depending on their species.

activities.prompt: Sort these animals by how they are born.
activities.explanation: Egg-laying animals hatch from eggs. Live-bearing animals are born from their mother's body.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about the caterpillar.
activities.explanation: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly.
activities.sentence: As it grows, a caterpillar becomes a ___ with wings.

activities.prompt: Hugo watches a video of a tadpole. Which change will he see before it becomes an adult frog?
activities.explanation: A tadpole grows small legs. Later, it loses its tail.
activities.hint: Think about how frogs swim and jump.

activities.prompt: Which statement about animals is incorrect?
activities.explanation: Not all young animals look just like their parents. A tadpole looks different from a frog.
activities.hint: Remember how frogs and caterpillars change.
options: All young animals look exactly like their parents at birth

activities.prompt: Read the text and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: A caterpillar becomes a chrysalis before a butterfly emerges. We observe animals without harming them.
activities.title: Aisha's caterpillar
activities.text: Aisha watches a green caterpillar in the garden without touching it. It eats fresh leaves. Later, it becomes a chrysalis. Its body changes during this stage. Then a butterfly comes out and flies away. Aisha keeps watching with her teacher.

questions.explanation: The text says the caterpillar eats fresh leaves.

questions.prompt: What does the caterpillar become in the end?
questions.explanation: A butterfly comes out of the chrysalis.

activities.prompt: Put the stages of a butterfly's life cycle in order.
activities.explanation: First comes the egg, then the caterpillar, chrysalis and adult butterfly.
